memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "On the seventh day the priest is to examine them again, and if the sore has faded and has not spread in the skin, the priest shall pronounce them clean; it is only a rash. They must wash their clothes, and they will be clean." - Lev 13:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
It is only a rash.

After fourteen days of watching and worrying, the verdict comes: this was not what you feared. Wash your clothes. Go home. You are clean.

We should let that land, because so much of our mental energy is spent on things that turn out to be only a rash. The message we replayed a hundred times that meant nothing. The symptom that was harmless. The conversation we were dreading that went perfectly well. The financial worry that resolved itself. Anxiety is expensive, and much of what it charges us is for troubles that never arrive.

Jesus knew this about us. Can any one of you by worrying add a single hour to your life? he asked (Matt 6:27). Not a rebuke — an observation. Worry does not work. It has never once solved the thing it circles around.

That does not mean every alarm is false. Some spots really are serious, as this chapter goes on to show. The point is not that nothing is ever wrong. The point is that we are not the ones who have to carry the verdict. There is a Priest who examines, and a Father who knows what we need before we ask (Matt 6:8).

Some of what you are carrying today is only a rash.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What are you worrying about that may well turn out to be nothing?
2. How much of your energy this week went to imagined outcomes?
3. What would it look like to hand today's uncertainty to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I spend so much strength on troubles that never come. Teach me to bring my fears to You each day and to leave the verdict in Your hands. Amen.
